title: Research Trends in Organic Waste Management in Municipal Marketplaces
author: Nicolas Norena

steps.title: Define Search Parameters and Criteria
steps.instruction: Establish the inclusion and exclusion criteria for the bibliometric analysis to ensure data quality and relevance.

substeps.instruction: Include original research articles, systematic reviews, book chapters, and conference proceedings published between 2000 and 2023.
Limit language to English, Spanish, or Portuguese.
Require papers to explicitly address organic waste management in municipal markets or similar urban areas.
Exclude editorials, letters to the editor, brief notes, and non-peer-reviewed articles.
Exclude studies focusing exclusively on industrial or agricultural waste, or general waste management without a specific focus on market organic waste.

steps.title: Execute Database Search
steps.instruction: Perform a literature search in the Scopus database using a specific Boolean search equation.

substeps.instruction: Implement the search equation: (“organic waste” OR “food waste” OR “biodegradable waste” OR “organic residues” OR “municipal solid organic waste” OR “green waste” OR “compostable waste”) AND (“marketplaces” OR “markets” OR “farmer’s market” OR “bazaar” OR “public market” OR “local market” OR “street market”) AND (“valorization” OR “waste management” OR “composting” OR “recycling” OR “waste utilization” OR “resource recovery” OR “bioconversion” OR “circular economy” OR “sustainability” OR “environmental impact” OR “waste-to-energy” OR “upcycling” OR “material recovery”) AND (“municipal” OR “city” OR “urban” OR “local government” OR “civic” OR “metropolitan” OR “town” OR “municipality”) AND NOT (“wastewater” OR “agricultural waste” OR “industrial waste”).

steps.title: Screen and Filter Publications
steps.instruction: Apply a PRISMA-based screening framework to select the final dataset of publications.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve records from Scopus using the predefined search equation.
Remove duplicate records and studies not directly related to organic waste management in municipal marketplaces via title and abstract evaluation.
Perform full-text assessment to verify eligibility based on inclusion/exclusion criteria.
Export the final dataset (206 publications) in .CSV format, including titles, authors, affiliations, keywords, abstracts, number of citations, countries of publication, and journals.

steps.title: Process and Analyze Bibliometric Data
steps.instruction: Use Bibliometrix (R package) and VOSviewer to perform quantitative and visual analyses.

substeps.instruction: Use Bibliometrix for quantitative analysis of annual publication trends, author productivity, journal distribution, and country contributions.
Apply keyword normalization to standardize synonyms and translate non-English keywords into English.
Generate co-occurrence and co-authorship matrices within Bibliometrix.
Use VOSviewer for network visualization and mapping of co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, and international collaboration patterns.
Apply association strength normalization and clustering algorithms in VOSviewer to identify thematic structures.

steps.title: Evaluate Research Metrics and Trends
steps.instruction: Analyze the processed data to identify key trends, influences, and thematic structures.

substeps.instruction: Analyze publications per year for temporal trends.
Rank authors by number of publications to measure influence.
Analyze journal productivity by number of articles and impact.
Evaluate global geographical distribution of scientific production.
Perform keyword co-occurrence analysis to identify research clusters (e.g., composting, circular economy).
Construct a strategic diagram to classify themes by density and centrality into motor themes, basic themes, niche themes, and emerging/declining themes.
Analyze cross-country and author co-authorship networks to evaluate collaboration dynamics.
